correctness.rationale: Ordinary nonempty spheres are exactly radius-zero singleton sets and sibling shells (union of all children except the center child) at positive internal-node radius. For support {x,y}, singletons give traces and a containing shell exists except when LCA is binary root and pair crosses root children; s2=C(N,2)-1_{binary root} n1 n2. A shattered triple must be equilateral and choose three child branches at node v; containing/empty shells exist iff v is nonroot or root has >=4 children, giving s3=sum nonroot E3(v)+1_{root >=4}E3(root). Any four-support would need all triples equilateral, but a sibling shell cannot select exactly two of four distinct equal-distance branches, so s>=4=0. Covers N=1 and N=2 edge cases; full-b-ary formulas follow counting nodes. Fresh independent distance-sphere computations on nine hierarchies up to eight leaves matched pair, triple and four-support counts. Source verifier was inspected; its claimed all-405-shape computation was not rerun.
residual_risks: The supplied 405-hierarchy count was not independently repeated; independent checks cover nine representative shapes, while all-size result rests on the exact-shell proof.
